workspace.title: Papers and Post-its
workspace.description: Preferences on this computer for thinking and remembering without interrupting work.
workspace.desktopHint: Hide windows without completing or deleting notes. Enable again to restore them.
workspace.pinNewHint: Disable to create stored notes and pin them when needed.
workspace.paperHint: Save up to six pens in the side atelier. Plain, grid, ruled, dotted and light/dark backgrounds belong to each Paper and are changed with Background in the editor.

tags.title: Tags
tags.description: Create reusable contexts. Name and color changes appear immediately on related tasks.
tags.empty: No tags yet. Praxis can also create a tag when you type + in a task title.

create.title: Create your first Paper
create.body: Open Papers and create a free sheet. Group Papers in notebooks by project or subject. Content thumbnails help you recognize each idea.
create.caption: The library brings all your Papers together. New Paper opens a blank canvas, and its header name identifies your ideas.

draw.title: Draw and choose a stroke
draw.body: Use the side atelier to choose a pen, pencil, graphite, fountain pen or ink. Color, width and adjustments are in the top bar. Pause at the end of a stroke to regularize shapes when Hold to correct is enabled.
draw.caption: Tools in the side atelier; adjustments in the top bar.

text.title: Write and highlight ideas
text.body: Choose Text and edit freely. Pick one of four quick sizes, bold, italic, color and alignment. Select a passage to underline, circle or highlight with hand-drawn annotations and choose their color.
text.caption: Text can remain transparent over the sheet. In Adjust stroke, you can also choose a rectangle or oval background and position text inside it.

organize.title: Arrange and navigate the sheet
organize.body: Select with a click, box or lasso. Group elements through the context menu and align with smart guides. Control visibility and locking in layers; save drawings to your personal library for reuse in other Papers.
organize.caption: Handles identify the selection. Position, size and rotation let you reorganize ideas without drawing them again.

link.title: Connect a Paper to a task
link.body: A Paper can stand alone or link to several tasks. Linking preserves the same drawing without creating copies. Task notes hold written context; tasks still own dates, checklists and reminders.
link.caption: The link points to the same Paper without creating a copy. Dates, checklists and reminders still belong to the task.

share.title: Save, focus and share
share.body: Use focus mode to fill the workspace. Define scenes and present with the laser pointer, or export your drawing. Background offers plain, grid, ruled or dotted sheets in light or dark appearance.
share.caption: Export creates an image of the Paper content to share with your team. The editable document remains in your vault.

papers.title: How to use a Paper
papers.description: Papers are infinite digital sheets for writing, drawing and organizing ideas. The Portuguese name is Papéis.
papers.roles: A task defines what to do. Notes record information in text. A Paper gives you space to explore ideas visually. A reminder tells you when to return to the task.
steps: Open Papers and create a sheet, even before defining a task.
Draw, write and arrange your ideas on the canvas. Changes are saved in your vault.
When an idea becomes an action, create or open a task and link the Paper in its details.
papers.reuse: One Paper can support several tasks. Removing a link keeps the sheet in the library; completing a task preserves your ideas too.
papers.exampleBody: Explore screens, paths and questions in a Paper.
papers.exampleTask: Then link this Paper to the task “Implement sign-up” to work with the context at hand.

help.title: How to use Praxis
help.intro: Explore ideas in Papers, preserve context in notes and turn what matters into tasks and reminders.
help.shortcutFree: Create a task without a preset context

access.title: Open your vault
access.description: The .praxis file is the source of your data. It stays local and encrypted, including when stored in a folder synchronized by you.
steps: Select an existing .praxis file or choose where to create a new vault.
Enter the password. Content opens only after the correct password is validated.
Use Lock to close the vault. While it is unlocked, closing the window keeps reminders and the badge active.

capture.title: Create without losing context
capture.description: Praxis supports contextual and context-free creation, so you can capture quickly while retaining control over dates, reminders, notes, tags, and checklists.
capture.contextLabel: Uses the current screen and selected day as context.
capture.contextBody: In My Day, the task is due today. In My Week, it receives the day selected in the calendar.
capture.freeLabel: Opens a task without a preset date.
capture.freeBody: Use it when you want to define every detail manually or simply capture an open task without a deadline.

views.title: Use each view to answer one question
views.description: Views are not folders. Each one answers a practical question and loads only the tasks it needs.
views.today: What is overdue, due today, or completed today.
views.week: The next seven days, starting tomorrow.
views.pending: Everything still open, grouped by urgency.
views.reminders: Only pending tasks with a notification configured.

reminder.title: Due dates and reminders serve different purposes
reminder.description: A due date defines urgency and lateness. A reminder defines when Windows should call your attention.
steps: Set a due date to indicate when the task must be ready.
Set a reminder only when you want a notification at a specific time.
Keep notifications enabled in Praxis settings and in Windows.
reminder.exampleNote: Due at 4:00 PM with a reminder thirty minutes earlier.

details.title: Break work down without creating new obligations
details.description: Checklists and tags enrich a task, but only the parent task has a due date, reminder, recurrence, and badge participation.
details.checklist: Use a checklist for visual steps. When every item is completed, the parent task is completed automatically.
details.tags: Use tags to identify contexts such as work, personal, or finance. Renaming or recoloring a tag updates every related task.
details.inlineTag: When creating or editing a task, type + in the title to search for a tag. If it does not exist, confirm with Enter to create and assign it automatically.

lifecycle.title: Complete, reopen, or restore
lifecycle.description: Praxis preserves the task lifecycle so its history remains useful without occupying working views.
lifecycle.toggle: Click the task indicator to switch between pending and completed.
lifecycle.archive: Older completed tasks can be archived automatically according to the policy selected in Settings.
lifecycle.restore: In Archived, use the blue restore icon beside the trash button. The original completion date is preserved.

privacy.title: Adjust the app without exposing your vault
privacy.description: Settings includes appearance, notifications, badge, startup, retention, and safe technical indicators.
privacy.database: Database status shows whether the vault is open, when the file was updated, and whether encryption is active, without revealing the password or content.
privacy.theme: Choose Paper, Dark, Sepia, Forest, or Midnight in Settings. Each palette keeps task priorities visually distinct.

help.supportTitle: Built with care, supported by people who believe in it
help.supportDescription: Meet the person behind Praxis and, if it makes sense to you, help keep the project moving forward.
help.supportVisualBody: Support funds development and maintenance, not barriers for people who simply need to organize their day.
help.supportVisualNote: Local privacy, reliable reminders, and a calm experience remain at the center of the product.
help.footerTitle: Ready to get back to work
help.footerBody: Think, keep the context and take the next step.

postits.title: Post-its: remember, resolve, complete
postits.description: Free notes independent from tasks, reminders and Papers. No date required and no notification scheduling.
postits.newShortcut: New note in the Post-its section
postits.preferences: Settings → Papers and Post-its defines initial color, pinning and window limit. In Post-its, select notes to group them into piles; search also finds grouped content.
postits.exampleBody: Gather ideas for the next conversation.

capture.title: Create and pin
capture.body: Open Post-its and use New Post-it or Alt+N. Text saves automatically. Finish with Ctrl+Enter or Escape: the note automatically folds into a small titled tab.
capture.caption: Click the illustrated tab to reveal the content. Additional notes wait in the queue.

edit.title: Edit in the note
edit.body: Hover or focus the tab to preview it. Click or press Space to read; Enter, double-click or Edit opens editing in the same window. Escape saves and folds the note. These states are automatic, with no mode settings.
edit.caption: Try Edit: this illustration only changes the demo, leaving your vault untouched.

done.title: Complete and move on
done.body: When finished, click Done on the desktop or in Post-its. The window disappears. You can reopen the note for seven days, then it is removed from the active vault. If the vault is closed at expiry, cleanup runs when it opens again.
done.caption: Active notes do not expire. Completed notes have seven-day retention independent from task archives.

support.intro1: Praxis is independently created and maintained by {name}, with special attention to privacy, performance, and the details that make daily use calmer.
support.intro2: If Praxis helps you remember what matters, a voluntary contribution supports development, Windows testing, and the project’s continuity. Praxis will continue to work normally without a donation.
support.internationalDescription: Support Praxis through Buy Me a Coffee in your system browser.
